blocks.text: In the debate of state law, the most fundamental question is not who benefits or is harmed, but whether the principle of law is applied consistently.
The healthy state of law is not measured by the stability of a person's position, but by the courage of a judicial institution to apply the same standard to similar substantial situations.

The decree of Constitution Number 90 / PUU-XXI / 2023 and the case of the President's Elections Number 01 / PHPU.PRES.XXIV / 2026 form a series of interrelated constitutional events. Both of which involve the run-in process of Gibran Rakaking in the 2024 election.

The question is simple but sharp: if the Constitution Court's office of authority changes the conditions of the candidacy through the 90 verdict, why does it come to a plea that tests the validity of the same nomination process?
The verdict that Change the Rule of Play

The verdict of Number 90 / PUU-XXI / 2023 in real time changed the interpretation of Article 169 letters q. The court states that minimum age rule of 40 years goes against the 1945, as long as it is not defined as a 40-year-old abuse or ever / sitting in a select post by the election, including the local chief.
This verdict has a huge state impact. It doesn't just interpret norms, it creates new conditions that allow someone who was previously unqualified to be a member of the 2024 election.

The controversy surrounding the ruling includes issues of strong interest conflict and dissenting opinion not removing the fact that the court has placed itself at the center of a changing rules of nomination.
Retest the same process
In September 2026, Denny Indrayana and a number of applicants filed a case against President No. 01 / PHAS.PRES-XXIV / 2026.

The object of this case is the fulfilment of Gibran Rakabuming's education condition during the candidacy of the vice president, especially related to Article 169 of the Election Act and the document of the award for education.

This case has been diagnosed and entered the inspection phase. KPU, Bawaslu, as well as related parties are asked to give a statement. The petitioners asked the court to examine the substance, not simply reject it on the basis of a systematic delay.
This is where the constitutional tension arose.

Part of the party thinks that the status of officials who have voted for the election, is set to be winners, and sworn to be no longer to be questioned because it can create uncertainty in the law. Such concerns are understandable.
But the same logic must be tested consistently against previous events.

If the 90 verdict can be used to open a person's nomination door, then when there comes a plea related to the validity of the same candidacy process, the court cannot by a priori shut down. The court is at the center of a series of constitutional events.
It doesn't mean every suit has to be granted. The most important thing is objective test substance.
Do the charges filed have strong legal basis?
Is there a constitutional violation that can be proven?
If it's not proven, it's over.
But if proven, the state of law should not turn a blind eye just because the issue is considered systematic or potentially destructive to stability.

A healthy state of law must maintain balance between the certainty of law and justice. The certainty without truth is risky to empty formalities. Instead, a search for truth without procedure can turn into authority.
In the end, that must be maintained not in the least of a person's stability, but in the public belief that the principle of law is applied consistently to anyone and under any circumstances.
In constitutional countries, the measure of justice is not who wins or loses, but whether the same principle is applied to the same situation.
The Constitution Court is now faced with the trials.
The way the court answers it will determine not only the fate of one thing, but also the quality of this agency's commitment to constitutional consistency.
Doctor. Hanny Per
